comment: Three supplier invoices, seeded WITHOUT running the capture pipeline. Reaching EXTRACTED normally needs rasterization, local OCR, PII masking, a vision call and a running worker; the seeder instead calls apFlowDocumentService.savePipelineResult with the canned results below, which lands a genuinely EXTRACTED document - real rows, real FSM transition, real audit trail - with no API key and no worker. Uploading a fresh invoice through the UI still exercises the real pipeline when a key is configured. Amounts are decimal strings and are parsed through parseMoneyText at load, exactly as they would be coming off a vision model, so no float ever touches a cents value. `arithmeticOk` is the extractor's own subtotal + tax = total check and must agree with the numbers here, or the seeded document would claim a validation state its own data contradicts.

pageImage.comment: No binary blobs are committed. The seeder renders a plain invoice-looking PNG per document with sharp (a dependency since Phase 10) from the values below, writes it through storageService.put, and uses the returned SHA-256 as the page's redactedSha256. That keeps the repo text-only while still producing real bytes an auditor can open from the ledger line, and the image genuinely matches what the extraction claims.

documents.outcomeComment: Posted through postingService so the AP-Flow -> LedgerCore link is visible end to end: the journal entry carries source_type 'ap_flow' and the source document's SHA-256, so an auditor can walk from a ledger line back to the original image.

Left EXTRACTED so the review queue is not empty. Its second line is deliberately low-confidence and unmapped, which is exactly the case the human-in-the-loop screen exists for - a reviewer picks the account before it can post.

Subtotal plus tax does NOT equal the printed total - a real and common defect on a scanned invoice. arithmeticOk is false and the mismatch is recorded in validationErrors, so the review screen shows the extractor refusing to paper over a document it could not reconcile. This is the honest-failure case; without it the demo only ever shows the happy path.
